drawing.svg: 26 shapes, 2605 bytes
pelican 7.0/10: The long bill and big throat pouch make it clearly a pelican, which meets the 7 anchor. It misses higher scores because the body is a plump, duck-like oval, the legs are plain sticks and the feet are tiny wedges that are not visibly webbed.
craft 7.0/10: The shapes are tidy and the palette is pleasant, which is the 7 anchor. It is not poster-quality: the legs are rigid sticks, the feet are crude triangles, the wing awkwardly covers the handlebar, the tail is a plain wedge, and there is no ground or setting.
[cli:claude] Redraw the feet as large orange webbed pelican feet clamped onto the pedals, and add a visible handlebar with the wing tip curled around it. This makes the bird more clearly a pelican and the riding more convincing at the same time.

pelican.evidence: No text exists in the artifact to quote. Visual evidence: a white bird with an S-curved neck, an eye, a long yellow upper bill over a large, darker yellow throat pouch, a grey wing with feather strokes, a grey tail wedge, orange stick legs and small yellow wedge feet.
pelican.why: The long bill and big throat pouch make it clearly a pelican, which meets the 7 anchor. It misses higher scores because the body is a plump, duck-like oval, the legs are plain sticks and the feet are tiny wedges that are not visibly webbed.

bicycle.evidence: No text exists in the artifact to quote. Visual evidence: two dark wheels with 8 light spokes and grey hubs, a teal diamond frame (top tube, down tube, seat tube, seat stay and chainstay), a fork to the front hub, a black saddle, a chainring with a crank arm and two black pedals, and grey chain lines running to the rear hub.
bicycle.why: It is a complete and mechanically plausible bike with the frame, spokes, hubs, chain, crank and pedals the top anchor asks for. It falls short of 10 because the handlebar is only a short black stub mostly hidden by the wing, there is no rear cog, and the chain is just two thin lines.

riding.evidence: No text exists in the artifact to quote. Visual evidence: the pelican's body rests directly on the black saddle, each orange leg bends at the joint and ends with a yellow foot on one of the two pedals at opposite crank positions, and the wing tip reaches forward to the handlebar.
riding.why: It is seated, with feet on the pedals and the wing on the handlebar, so it meets most of the 10 anchor. The pose is static, though: the body is upright and stiff, there are no motion cues, and the wing seems to rest over the bar rather than grip it.

craft.why: The shapes are tidy and the palette is pleasant, which is the 7 anchor. It is not poster-quality: the legs are rigid sticks, the feet are crude triangles, the wing awkwardly covers the handlebar, the tail is a plain wedge, and there is no ground or setting.
